classification_reasons: Blast radius: a new eight-module package (app/data/, about 1,200 lines), the project's first runtime dependency (polars), new external inputs from three Binance hosts, a new on-disk cache layout and a CLI; no risk-list item is touched.
Test coverage: no existing test covers any of this; every proof test is new in this change (19 Proof tests plus parametrised unit tests).

Spec tightness: acceptance is measurable and the three design concerns are closed by the panel, but the build added three choices the spec does not cover (DownloadError on exhausted retries, REST days cached only when complete, the 'Vision refused (HTTP n)' gap) and one departure (ci.yml not edited).
attempted: Intent: checked each intent outcome against the code. Vision spot and um URLs (vision.py day_url, MARKET_PATHS); REST fill on 404 only (loader.sync_days: only NOT_ON_VISION days go to _rest_pass); gaps raised, never hidden (KlineGapError with .gaps and .frame); polars frame sorted with unique open_time (per-day _on_grid, then concat in day order); ignore column dropped; the µs/ms split detected per column, floored to ms; Parquet-only zstd-3 cache with atomic writes; cache=False; the 4-thread pool; 10 s/60 s timeouts (_HTTPSConnection.connect); 3 retries at 1/2/4 s plus jitter; Retry-After; 418; urllib only; injectable Fetch. Nothing found that solves a nearby problem instead of the stated one.

Spec and plan: the diff stays inside plan.md 'Files that change'. The two departures, tests/binance_stub.py added and ci.yml dropped, are written into plan.md in this same diff, as REVIEW.md requires. The spec's Gaps reasons, A1-A12, panel #1 (missing weight header waits 1 s; test_weight_pacer and test_rest_waits_when_weight_header_is_missing), panel #2 (scripts/measure_storage.py committed, its output in evidence/storage-measurement.md, +15.4% under the 20% reopen rule) and panel #3 (the exact two-candle gap test) are all implemented.

Spec gap left to the owner (not a park): spec Design 'Dependencies and CI' and the intent say .github/workflows/ci.yml must install polars. The build could not edit .github/ and recorded this as a departure in plan.md Risks. Until the owner adds polars==2.1.0 to the 'Install the toolchain' step, the project CI's 'python -m pytest' fails at collection (ModuleNotFoundError: polars in tests/test_data.py) on this PR and on main after merge, and that raises the maintain metric ci_test_failure_rate. The SDLC runner is unaffected (sdlc.yaml commands.setup installs polars). The run cannot do this itself; the owner can.

Proof: test.log, build.log and lint.log do not exist yet, and verifier.md says this is a CI session (SDLC_GATE_COMMANDS=runner), with the three targets read rather than run. That is the case the runner covers, so I left it to the runner. Instead I traced every test in tests/test_data.py and tests/test_data_cli.py against the code by hand: expected sleeps (1.25/2.25/4.25 with jitter fixed at 0.25; 15.0 at wall clock 45 s into the minute; 7.0 for Retry-After), REST page counts (10/10/4, then one empty page; 3 calls when the range ends exactly), gap boundaries, CLI line formats and exit codes. I found no test that would fail. tests/ has no __init__.py, so pytest's default prepend import mode puts tests/ on sys.path and 'from binance_stub import ...' resolves. The verifier report exercises the changed behaviour through the stub (loads, the gap shapes, the 418 cancellation, retries, the CLI) and also the real entry point with python -m app.data.

Blast radius: no existing caller (app/__init__.py and test_smoke.py are untouched; __version__ stays 0.1.0, matching pyproject). pyproject gains only the dependency. No guardrail file is in the diff (.claude/**, CLAUDE.md, REVIEW.md, sdlc.yaml, policies/**). No migration, and the cache sits outside the repo by default. risk-hits is empty, and none of auth, data migrations, money movement or production config applies. Under REVIEW.md, CLAUDE.md is now stale in two places, the Setup line ('pip install pytest ruff') and the healthy test output ('1 passed'). plan.md Risks records both for the owner, since the run cannot edit CLAUDE.md.

Policies: security-baseline rule 2 holds. Symbol, interval, market and dates are validated before any URL or path is built (make_request; the tests check zero fetches); the query is built with urlencode. day_path resolves the path and refuses one outside <cache>/binance-vision. The zip body is capped at 64 MiB, the member at 256 MiB with a bounded read(), and only the expected member is read, in memory. The SHA-256 is checked against .CHECKSUM before parsing. The REST JSON shape is checked (int times, string numbers, finite floats), and a malformed body becomes a gap. clear_cache deletes only regular, non-symlink files whose name matches the exact day-file pattern and whose resolved path is inside the subtree. Rule 6 holds: TLS verification stays on (HTTPSConnection with the default context), with no eval, exec, pickle or shell. Rule 3: no secrets. data-conventions: public market data, schema defined once in schema.py. coding-standards: polars has its Risks line; test_data.py is 496 lines, under 500.

Untrusted-input edge (nit, not a park): an integer field too large for Int64 in a CSV row or REST row parses with int() but then fails in pl.DataFrame(). The error would likely be OverflowError or a polars error, not MalformedDataError or ValueError, so it escapes the gap handling and fails the load with a traceback. It needs a checksum-matching file or a TLS-served body from Binance itself, so the risk is low.

Gaps and grid: _expected_ms covers the whole interval grid for closed days and, for today, only candles with open+interval <= now. The same now goes to sync_days and find_gaps. Consecutive missing candles with the same reason merge across day boundaries. The reasons separate a day absent from both sources from candles missing inside a file (CACHED and VISION) or inside a REST answer. A Vision file holding off-grid rows has them dropped by _on_grid. I found no off-by-one: endTime is end_ms-1, inclusive in ms, and next_ms is last_open + interval.

REST paging: one range per run of consecutive Vision-404 days, sequential in the main thread after the Vision pass. An empty page ends the range. A page that does not advance is 'unexpected REST response', so it cannot loop. Any non-200 that survives the retries ends the range with 'REST refused (HTTP n)'. 418 raises, and exhausted 429/5xx raises DownloadError (build choice a). The pacer waits before each call after the first: 80% of 6000 (spot) or 2400 (um) sleeps to the next minute boundary, and a missing or unparsable header waits 1 s.

Cache atomicity and clear safety: write_day writes a mkstemp file in the target directory, then os.replace, and unlinks the temp file on any BaseException. A SIGKILL can leave a hidden .tmp file, which the day-file pattern ignores (nit). read_day treats an unreadable file or a schema mismatch as absent, so the day is refetched. The current day is never read from or written to the cache. A REST day is cached only when complete (build choice b), a Vision day whenever it is non-empty, and an empty day never (A8).

Retries, 418 and cancellation: with_retries checks 418 before anything else, retries OSError and HTTPException (including URLError, timeouts and TLS errors), 429 and 5xx, honours numeric and HTTP-date Retry-After with max(backoff, retry_after), and stops when Retry-After exceeds 60 s. On any exception, _vision_pass sets the stop event (each guarded() call then raises _Cancelled) and shuts the pool down with cancel_futures=True. test_ban_stops_pending_vision_downloads bounds the calls at 8 over 20 days.

Behavior observation for the owner (not a park; the spec is silent): sync_days writes the cache only after both the Vision and REST passes finish. One DownloadError (retries exhausted, or Retry-After over 60 s) or a 418 anywhere in the range therefore discards every day already downloaded and verified in that run, and the rerun downloads them again. On the owner's own year-long check (730 Vision requests) this weakens the intent's 'each day is downloaded once' after a failure. The data stays correct and nothing partial is cached. Writing each closed day as it completes would close this; I name it so the owner can choose.

CLI exit codes: download returns 1 when any gap exists, otherwise 0. InvalidRequestError and DownloadError (including BinanceBanError and the long Retry-After) print one 'error:' line on stderr and return 2. argparse errors also exit 2. The tests cover invalid symbol, start date and interval, and the 418. An OSError from an unwritable cache directory, or a CachePathError from a symlinked market directory, is not caught and would show a traceback. Those are failures the spec does not list as expected (nit).

Tests that could pass with the bug present: I checked the gap test, which asserts exact start, end, candles, reason and the frame's rows and schema; spot equals futures (asserts frame equality and the futures URL); 'second load makes no fetch' (zero calls); 'cache=False' (asserts the call count triples, proving no read, and an empty directory, proving no write); 'current day not cached' (asserts hours 0-4, no file, and a refetch). Each would fail if its behaviour regressed. No pre-existing test is modified (change_type feature; test_smoke.py untouched).
Skip markers: none added in the diff (no pytest.mark.skip, skipif or xfail, no importorskip).

Claims against today's code: sdlc.yaml commands.setup is 'python -m pip install pytest ruff polars' in the working tree (spec claim true). ci.yml installs only pytest==9.1.1 and ruff==0.16.9 (true, and still true after this diff). app.__version__ is 0.1.0 and test_smoke.py pins it (true). pyproject had no dependencies before (removed lines: none) and requires-python >=3.10 (true). tests/ has no __init__.py (true, needed for the binance_stub import). No docs/decisions/index.md exists in the project, so there were no project decisions to check. The APIs used exist from Python 3.10: Path.is_relative_to, shutdown(cancel_futures=True), date.fromisoformat.
Drive: sdlc.yaml commands.drive is empty, so this angle does not apply.
